decisive_items: Regular rhythm with cannon A waves in the jugular venous waveform
QRS complexes outnumber P waves with 3:2 relationship
P-wave morphology shows negative deflection in leads II and aVF
response.rationale: Cannon A waves with negative P waves in II and aVF during a regular narrow-complex tachycardia are classic AVNRT features reflecting retrograde atrial activation. The 3:2 ventricular-to-atrial relationship also argues against atrial tachycardia, which requires atrial activity at least as frequent as ventricular activity.

rejected.why: Atrial tachycardia would be expected to have P waves at least as frequent as QRS complexes since atrial activity drives the ventricle; QRS outnumbering P waves (3:2) and cannon A waves are inconsistent with atrial tachycardia, while inferior-lead negative P waves are more compatible with retrograde atrial activation in AVNRT.
